$comment: The model roster. Copy this, edit it, and point ASSETSVC_MODELS at your copy — or mount it
from a ConfigMap, which is what the Helm chart does.
NOTHING IN assetsvc NAMES A VENDOR. Adapters are chosen by `kind` (see adapters.mjs) and the
rest is configuration: swapping flux.2 for another image server, or TRELLIS for another
reconstructor, is an entry here plus one environment variable, not a code change.
`url` is overridable per model at runtime by ASSETSVC_URL_<ID>, upper-cased with non-alphanumerics
as underscores — so `flux2-dev` reads ASSETSVC_URL_FLUX2_DEV. That is how the same roster serves
a laptop on port-forwards and a pod on cluster DNS without two files.

flux2-dev.$note: flux.2-dev takes its edit attachments under `image`; klein wants `image[]`. That is what `field` is for. On dev, everything in the attachment list is an EDIT SOURCE and is reproduced — `reference_image` as a style channel is klein-only and is silently discarded here.

flux2-klein.$note: Not deployed on gh200-1 today. Left here as the worked example of swapping an image model by configuration alone.

trellis2.$note: tools/recon-service. One GPU, one job at a time — it serialises internally, and assetsvc's own queue is concurrency 1 on the mesh lane so we do not race it into an out-of-memory. Send KEYED cut-outs: it keeps an alpha channel when one is present and our chroma key beats the background remover it would otherwise run.
